rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, pretrain_steps=0, n_iter=50, grad_clip=1.0, outer_wall_s=1400, per_scene_s=None, batch_size=1, lr=0.0003, optimizer=adam, unet_c=8, train_n=400, val_n=200, seed=42, rationale=iter-9 SIX-BOX. (1) PRIOR: iter-8 hr=0.0, stronger warm-start pretrain_epochs=10 gave rmse=0.00637, ssim=0.938 -- no better than ep=3; the amortised warm-start is ALSO over-smoothed, so entrenching it doesn't help. Best remains iter-6 (lr=3e-4, n_iter=50, c=16, ep=3, rmse=0.00628). Iters 1-8 all hr=0. (2) FAILURE MODE: plain-UNet N2I regresses to the over-smoothed FBP mean regardless of budget/capacity-up/warm-start strength/lr. (3) ONE KNOB: relative to iter-6 best reference, unet_c 16 -> 8 (both denoisers; ~0.12M params). iter-3 already tested c=32 (up); this tests c=8 (DOWN) to complete the capacity sweep. (4) HYPOTHESIS: a smaller-capacity denoiser has LESS ability to regress toward the smooth low-frequency mean, so it may leave more high-frequency structure intact and lower rmse; if hr rises, the denoiser was over-parameterized for the blur. Per the ceiling, more likely c=8 is simply a weaker denoiser that still cannot beat the FBP target and may even raise rmse (hr=0). Together with iter-3 (c=32) this brackets capacity: if BOTH c=8 and c=32 give hr=0, capacity is conclusively NOT the lever. (5) BUDGET: c=8 fast; pretrain ep=3 + 200*50-step fits + figure ~= 12 min << 30-min wall. (6) Loop continues; iter-10 self-dispatched. Reserved levers: n_iter=100 mid, grad_clip off, seed variance check, pretrain_steps cap, lr=1e-4 very gentle.
